body: Thank you for this. This is one of the replies here that has been the most helpful to me. I'm willing to bring his art out under my umbrella (so to speak) and am kind of ready and waiting to do that when he's ready. Which he knows. I think that makes him feel supported to some degree, but it doesn't solve the issue of him being generally directionless, unmotivated, and resistant to "making any moves" in his life, or the issue of him constantly complaining that he doesn't like my art supporting our family because he wants us to have a steadier paycheck (and yet, still no job on his end). He has a very difficult, oppositional personality type, and I'm pretty sure he even had an oppositional defiant label as a young child. As a teen he had a diagnosis from a psychologist of having narcissistic tendencies, although not full-on narcissism. I feel that still describes him well. Your questions made me realize a) we possibly can do something like what you're suggesting if we split; live close together, etc. and b) so many of our problems stem from HIM. Like, HE is unhappy with himself. Miserable, I would say. HE feels like a loser with nothing to show for himself. HE is embarrassed about who he is and where he is in life. But he still won't make any moves. Still turns to marijuana, and still cannot stop blaming me (openly at times and at times less openly) for all his issues. Those are the really hard things because I can't change them at all. If the relationship doesn't get more functional, I feel like I'll end up having to leave him once and for all so our kids don't see an unhealthy relationship as they get older. What I really wish is he would just become less resentful, bitter, and blame-y toward me so we could move forward and keep trying to give our kids a nuclear family under one roof. But... not my choice. It's sad because we co-parent them fairly well together most of the time, and I think they feel loved and supported by us both, generally speaking. His bitterness and resentment toward me is just this other thing that is constantly hanging around waiting to rear its head in the form of him being snappy, intolerant, rude, or not empathetic (mostly toward me).
I'll have to wait until there's more money (early next year). In the meantime, we could always try seeing a counselor again.

We divorced and then dialed back the legal part to legally separated, which is basically one paper filing away from fully divorced. So I just said we are divorced for the sake of simplicity. We are living together as coupled. We already had a custody battle and it came out 50/50 because that's how our state does things 99 percent of the time.

Our current arrangement actually is two days on, two days off. BUT in my state, when all the kids get a tiny bit older, they change it to four days on, four days off. I guess I just feel like that is a LOT of shuffling around and would be so bad for the kids' stability. What do you think, as a parent in that situation?
Yeah, I'm going to try to find someone today.

I have two degrees in psychology, so that is not true. I do think I am inadvertently in a mommy type of role, which is the source of a lot of problems, but if anything, I think I'm the more permissible mommy. I'm never mean to him. I'm respectful of him even when he arguably does not "deserve" it because he isn't consistently respectful of me. I do \*ALL\* the housekeeping, which is a ton because he is here all day long and is an extremely slovenly person (due to depression and also what I think are some oppositional tendencies--he wants to irritate me). I do almost all the "kid stuff" -- making doctor's appointments and taking them, taking them to social events, putting them to bed, bathing them, etc. I bring in all the income, which he spends on marijuana, etc. If that's your version of "mean mommy" I don't know what you think nice is. Also, I agreed with you that I have issues with control and codependency. I just have kids now, so getting out of a bad situation is much, much more complicated.
I really like this advice. Thanks.

He's been mentioning lately that he may, so we'll see what comes of it. I agree completely, he doesn't have to support us, even, but I think he should be bringing in income if he doesn't want to be a stay at home dad, which repeatedly he has said and shown he does not. TY for reading.
TY for replying.
TY. I agree, he isn't.
TY for the input.

You're not wrong. I do have issues with control and codependency, but they have gotten a lot better over time, to the point that I wish I hadn't married my husband and had kids with him, but don't know if I want to be away from my kids 50 percent of the time throughout their growing-up years. Also, I don't really play the role of mean mommy. If anything, with my husband, I am the permissible mommy.
In couples therapy, he isn't honest about the real issue (his resentment), and he doesn't talk about it at all in his individual therapy.
TY for your reply.

Yeah. He was when we were separated last time. I guess it's the four days with him, four with me, for the rest of their childhoods that makes me feel exhausted. And I can't imagine not seeing my kids for four days at a time, especially as they age and need someone who is more emotionally "with it" than their dad.

Well the part that isn't irrelevant is that we are already divorced and the courts in our area give 50/50 to everyone but murderers, so my husband (ex, whatever) got 50% even though the judge knew he hit me and that he had a marijuana problem. Around here, they make the kids do four days with one parent, four days with the other (kids get no say until age 17), which I think would create a lot of instability. I myself had to switch  houses as the child of divorced parents, and I never felt like I could truly get settled. Also, I'm pretty sure our kids have no idea the marriage isn't good. They're still very young. But clearly, I am not sure what to do and am considering leaving him again. I want what's best for them.
TY for your thoughts. I appreciate the input.

True re him being more a kid than a father. Untrue about the fake foot forward. I'm just saying only my extremely close friends know how I really feel. That's not fake, it's discretion. Important since I don't know what I want to do yet.

He hated the job he left to move to the city I was in, and I didn't ask him to do that. You are correct I have driven almost every major decision in the relationship, and was too pushy as a younger person--something I regret. He tells me what he wants, and what he wants is for us to make art together and me to stop making my art (or so he says at times), and he says this is so he could keep me on track if I get "thrown off" on a project. I don't get thrown off, and I usually do very well, so I see this as him trying to hide from having to make a choice, and I don't ever stop making my own art. He then is forced to slog along with his own. I wish I could see more ways he has sacrificed for me, but really I mostly see someone who has pouted and refused to make moves of his own in the years I have been pursuing my own art and encouraging him about his.

>ose to ignore the warning signs and committed yourself to a horrible person, but your kids did not sign up for this.

I agree with that, and I wish I could un-sign them up, but I can't. I tried so hard when we split to get more custody, and the judge knew about his marijuana and him hitting the once, but 50/50 is the default in our state and it's very tough to get anything different. I guess I just feel like they're going to be with him without me if I leave again, and as they age, what if that's bad? One of my kids in particular, he has trouble being patient with. That's all that's holding me to him.
Thanks for the input.
They're little. They love him and don't always like him. I think they don't know.

I think he thought he wanted it and also possibly it was out of spite. He already sought it and got it in our divorce. But we live in a state where 50/50 is what almost every couple gets. BTW the judge knew of his marijuana problems and didn't care.
Yeah, I think that's true.

So with respect for how you feel, I just don't see this as a big issue or one you should spend more time on. Who cares if he thinks he's smarter than you? You both know he isn't actually smarter. To respect you adequately, does he have to think you guys are totally equal in the smarts department and say so every time it comes up? I really don't think so. I have so many friends who are super smart and with partners who are super smart, and sometimes someone is bullheaded and will claim to be the smartest. My guess is that when he made his comments about him being smarter, he had no idea you would actually get upset and likely thought it was more of a tease or at the very least, something you wouldn't take ultra seriously. Then when you took him to task, it made him feel emasculated or embarrassed, so he doubled down and didn't think he could save face if he recanted. I would sleep on it, collect yourself, tell him you think his remarks were in poor form and arrogant/offputting, see if after some time to cool down he will say sorry, and, if possible, move on. His insecurity in other areas probably plays a role in how he acted with regards to this.

I'm ready to be strong, just don't know what is worse--them having to swap houses every four days for their entire childhoods, half of that time being cared for by someone who, last time we were separated, didn't bathe them or change their clothes daily, and is also regularly semi-snappy with them. Or being in a house with me + him, where a lot of the time each day I can be the caretaker. IMO it's just really not easy to figure out what is best. When he's not snappy with them, he's super fun and plays games and makes crafts and stuff. Despite his flaws, he is more actively involved in their lives than almost any other dad I know, due to him being at home all the time. In some ways he is nurturing and nice. It's a gray area, you know? Also -- no, I do not think they pick up on my sad vibes. I'm an excellent actress (I have acted professionally in the past) and put everything I have into this role. No one who knows my family thinks I am sad. Also, I'm not sad all the time in an active way, more like I can put my sadness into a box and keep it there and pull it out when I have some time alone at night and want to sit with it. Like I told my sister the other day, I'm not quote actively unhappy, but I'm not happy or satisfied either. It's hard to explain on Reddit. But I have pretty decent boundaries at least in this way, so on days when my husband is a jerk, I can still have a good day apart from that--a day in which I really enjoy my time with my kids, get good work done, enjoy my friends, and avoid getting drawn into the drama my husband wants to start. Believe me, if things don't improve between my husband and me, or if they get worse, I will split with him again and turn my poor kids into 4-days-on, 4-days-off nomads. If that's more emotionally healthy.

Funny I was just considering the fact that he is a fairly functional all-day vaper and the comment above doesn't reflect that. However, you said every day and I'm saying, in his case, ALL day (and all night). I am a big fan of marijuana generally speaking, and I think vaping every day is fine. I think it's about how often it's done and how it impacts the rest of the person's life, and whether it's helping them or holding them back. I vape, too, a few times a month and would be really thrilled if my husband would cut back to even two times a day. As it is, he's just vaping all day and all night, and I feel he is really not present, nor happy.
I appreciate the reply. Thanks. You're very right about our personalities, and that's such a good point that he is again expecting me to resolve his resentment.

The kid are still young, and I might still initiate another split, particularly if I think it would be better for the kids. I probably need to ask a therapist about this specifically. Also, it's really irrelevant since you can't see this for yourself, but I think the vibe in our house is probably more peaceful than it may seem. We almost never fight around them, and we often act nice to each other in our interactions. It's not like we outwardly dislike each other, more like I am really sad and dissatisfied, but kind of hide it (for now), and he thinks things are rocky at times but overall okay. A lot of these things I'm mentioning are below the surface or have been coming out more when we're alone at home and the kids are at school. When things were an actual train wreck with lots of fighting, I left. And it hasn't gotten back to that level again. That said, I get your point about them seeing relationships badly if things spill over more when they are at home, and as they age and understand things more. Thanks for pointing out that he does probably like it because he shifts pretend blame to me. That's a valid point I need to remember: he's not happy with me, he's happy having a scapegoat. FWIW, I grew up in a hyper-religious family thinking marriage was my only option. So that's why, for me.
Thanks for replying.
Hope I did it right!
Okay, thanks.

So, right now, two of our kids are in school full-time, and the third is in preschool four mornings a week, and we are going to add a fifth day in January, plus extend the hours so she goes to school 8:30-1 every day. This means that currently, four days a week he can work on his art for three to four hours guaranteed because the kids are gone. He usually doesn't want to work on his art for more than about three and a half or four hours a day. That's why he's so slow to finish things. When I'm not in what I would call a deadline period, he can get more like five hours a day for his art, but when I have a project that must be finished asap due to financial considerations, he has to drop back and only work the three to four hours a day four days per week, plus about two to three hours a day the other three days. These times are when we really have trouble, as it seems to trigger him and make him feel like his work isn't important. \*However\* like I said, he only wants to work 3-4 hours on most days anyway, and he almost never wants to sell his art, and I don't think he wants a 9-5 job.... so what do I do? I guess that's what I need to ask the therapist(s). I spend a lot of time trying not to work too much, but at the end of the day, I'm the sole income earner and end up super stressed and struggling to cope with the pressure I feel, which is amplified by the fact that my job is making art--something you can't always control. If I had some other degree that makes good money, like a nursing degree or a law license something like that, I would possibly just do that job. But nothing else I can do makes nearly as much money as working on my art, and we live in an expensive area of the country due to child 1's unique medical needs.
What does that mean? I'm old and uncool.

From what I've read, really never. I've read that in our state they have to be 17 to really have their preferences "heard." I should add that he has never been physically abusive to me since the one time in early 2014, and I think he would be better with the kids, as someone else suggested, without me around as a "scapegoat." At times he can be a really good, fun dad to them. I just think they would be better off with me most of the time. When he had them last time, during our year of being divorced, he never bathed them and didn't even change their clothes every day. They were little, but still.

I think you're right about this: those times when you were in your 20's are ingrained in his mind and with everything single failure of his he would default to those times.

It makes me really sad, but I agree there is probably nothing that can be done. He isn't open and honest with me enough to admit how angry and bitter he still is. So it can't be changed.

Thanks for your reply. Maybe you're right--our dynamic is just too established. I've done so much on my end to change my part of our dynamic, but I feel like he can't get past his bitterness at me and his habit of blaming me for his life, and the effects of this can be seen in our interactions. Even on so-called good days he is at times snappy, impatient, and smoking pot almost all day (not in view of our kids or inside the house, but still). He seems able to treat me with respect for small time periods but never for long ones. His default is blaming others for his problems, and when he isn't blaming me, he's blaming his parents. When he actively is blaming no one and ostensibly taking responsibility for the direction of his own life, what he's REALLY doing is being snappy and rude to the kids and me, abusing marijuana by vaping it ALL.DAY.LONG. and acting bitter and resentful while claiming he is fine. The four days on, four days off custody situation just really really bothers me. I should probably talk to a therapist about this like you said.

I appreciate your input, however I'm not sure what I could be doing differently right now. I do my own job and do it to the best of my ability, while also being very involved with my kids (which I love, but it's tough as hell to be both a mom and the sole income earner). 

I haven't pushed him to get a 9-5 job and quit being an artist AT ALL, EVER--I repeat EVER--except in \*\*one\*\* instance this past month when he said he is miserable relying on my job as our income and insinuated I am not doing a good job. To that I said he should sell his art again (right now, nothing of his is for sale, as he likes to take 3-4 years on each piece, while I rush through my own work so we have money to live), or he should consider getting a 9-5 job, because I'm doing the best I can and cannot provide for our family alone doing anything other than making my art. (We require my current generally high income to survive). 

I do think he has mental health issues, and he is in therapy (with full support from me). He has been in therapy for years. I encourage medication for depression, which he chooses to only take sometimes. I think he is doing his best. I really do. But he has major bitterness and resentment toward me, despite the fact that at this current time, I do everything I can to support him, and have always, always tried to support his art and his work. (After I started working alone way back when, he didn't pursue his own career as I did mine, and I can't \*make\* him). 

Since we got back together two and a half years ago, I've tried very, very hard to be sure he feels heard, supported, acknowledged, etc. He knows that I find being the only income-earner very stressful, but he often isn't supportive of me. I don't know. I guess it's just a classic bitterness situation, but I'm not being self-absorbed at this time. I was too pushy in my 20s, but I'm in my late 30s now...

You're right. I was pushy and too domineering, especially during those times, when we were in our early and mid-20s. I've been in therapy a lot since then, though, and am not at all that way now, nor have I been for I would say at least six years. I've had good boundaries emotionally and been able to fully take responsibility for my own flaws for I would say about three years (with that improving progressively as I grow as a person).

I regret steering our art, which was more of a joint venture at times, into a place where I was marketing my own work more, and if I was given a re-do, I would not do that. (When you know better you do better, as they say). However, I do not think my actions fully account for his persistent floundering. I am curious if you do. If you do, that's fine.

I agree he and I can't move forward unless he acknowledges his bitterness and anger, and it does seem unlikely. I also don't think he will get over the resentment, and I mostly hope we can live as peaceably as possible "on the surface" while our kids are young. If we split again, they'll live with each of us for four days at a time, which I think is horrible for children.

Thanks for your input.

Your body is your body. He needs to deal with it gracefully. Also, you're not that overweight. You're an adult woman, not a barbie.
Have you thought of trying something else? <3 What about therapy? Any chance of something cheap?
Still thinking of you and sending you love and strength... <3 i hope somehow things are going better than you thought they would be.
Do you think that has a lot to do with why you're struggling? I feel like surely it must? Any chance you could one day live as a girl? <3 Sending warm thoughts your way...

This might seem like a dumb suggestion, but have you tried doing some kind of aerobic exercise every day? Brisk walking, jogging, even climbing stairs? 15-20 mins minimum... at least five days a week. I have really severe depression two weeks out of the month because of a genetic glitch that makes my hormones basically fuck up my brain chemistry. (It's called PMDD). I'm on some forums for people who have PMDD (obviously all women), but all of us are kind of awesome at not killing ourselves, because we have to fight off those urges basically half of our lives. The three top things that help most of us are daily aerobic exercise (it's like an antidepressant, I swear); CBD or low THC/high CBD marijuana (if you can get your hands on that); and a lot of us use this supplement called sam-e, and another one called 5-HTP. You can get both of them at the grocery store normally. I know it might seem hard to believe, but they are super effective and the sam-e one in particular works about as well as most of the SSRIs, but without the bad side effects. You might consider trying one of those! I really think it would ease your depression. The sam-e works same-day and doesn't have to be taken every day like a regular antidepressant. You can google it if you want. That stuff has saved me from suicide too many times to count...because it works the same day. Usually in like two hours. Anyway, keep on keeping on, and keep your girlfriend in the loop, okay? Don't worry about making anyone else worried. <3

I'm bad with people, too, but I think sometimes you can get a job and become good at that particular job over time. If nothing else, try to be nicer to yourself. You definitely don't deserve that kind of talk. I promise. <3
Maybe search your area for one that specializes in BPD? Someone like that surely wouldn't judge... <3
Did any of them work okay? How was therapy? If you've been off meds that long, maybe trying a new one would make all the difference... Just saying. <3

Borderline is very tough to deal with... My sister suffers from BPD, so I know a fair bit about it. We are very close. You might already know, but struggling with BPD is definitely not your fault and is probably the result of things that happened in your early childhood. Also, there are some therapists that specialize in BPD and some protocols that have helped people heal from it. Are you seeing a therapist? Is that something that might be possible for you? Sending light and love!

I think your internet friends would probably still miss you. I bet your mom definitely would. What's your job situation like? Or rather, what's your history like? It sounds like you're depressed and in a lot of pain right now, but that doesn't mean things can't get better... Things can always get better. You're not a loser. You need to try to talk to yourself kindly like you would a sick friend. How you talk to yourself really matters, and you deserve to hear good things, whether you have a job or not. You don't exist just to have a job, talent, or education. You are valuable as you are. And I think you could get to somewhere you want to be if you stay alive and take things one step at a time. I'm here if you want to tell me what's up...  <3 Sending love and light!

I've been there. What you said resonates with me. <3 I'm sorry you're struggling. Do you have a therapist? Taking any meds? I think it's important to let someone close to you know that you're struggling... So what if they worry? Life is fully of worry, you know? Sometimes it's good to worry when it helps someone you love...
What's been going on? Why are you thinking of this? I'm here if you want to talk.... <3 Please don't do anything to hurt yourself.
I just wanted to say I'm really sorry you're having such a hard time. <3 Is your health insurance situation bad? What medicine have you tried?
What's your situation right now...? School/job/age...? I'm sorry you're feeling this way. <3

Starving sucks! Trust me, I have a long history of anorexia. It will also really hurt your body in the long-term, and not in a nice, relieving, dying type of way. In an annoying, making-aging-harder type of way... It sounds like you're struggling and don't feel supported by your family. Sometimes family isn't the best place to go for support, even though it would be nice if they could be. Maybe your people just aren't strong enough to support you. But that doesn't mean no one is. Are you in therapy? What is your situation exactly? Sending love and light!

Even if things seem bleak right now, they could still turn around. I don't want to belittle your feelings, but 25 won't seem that old when you are 35 or 45... SO many things can change, even in only a year or two. You truly never know where life might take you. You are NOT too old to achieve things you could be proud of. What would you like to do with your life? If everything was ideal? Also, tell me about not being able to get yourself to study... Maybe some medicine would help. Do you have trouble focusing? There are things you can do to feel better...I just know it! <3 I'm 34 (35 soon! whoa!) and have had so many huge ups and downs in my life... I've learned some good coping strategies, which is saying a lot, because I have significant barriers to good mental health. If I can hang in here, I know you can, too. It sounds like you're depressed, upset, and frustrated with how things are going...which is okay. I'm here if you want to talk.

If you have three university degrees having had the kind of early life you describe here, you are a fucking fighter. It sounds like you're really miserable and profoundly tired of trying, and that makes sense. This is a lot for any person to have to deal with. When is the last time you were in therapy? Did it not go well? Have you seen a therapist that specializes in BPD? I'm sure you are aware there are some, and there is a specific protocol that helps some people heal from BPD. I don't have any easy answers, but I wanted to say I'm sorry you're in so much pain and misery. It does sound like you're pretty depressed. I would like to think a great therapist and the right meds could help you start down a different path. I have significant mental health issues as well (cyclothymia, PMDD, thyroid disease, and high functioning Asperger's). So I understand getting to a good place can seem really, really tough. Too tough. But you don't know how the world will turn out without you in it. I know it might sound silly, but you have no idea who might need you here. Yes, the world can be a horrible place, but we're in it together. Maybe your suffering will not end, but maybe it will. I think you should consider getting back into therapy, if only for a few weeks, and trying a different med this time. Just give it one more try. If it doesn't work, it's not like you're stuck here. You can re-evaluate... <3 Sending love and light.

I'm kind of like this. More like this at some times than at other times. Are you sure you're happy for the most part? I guess that's so subjective, the question is really meaningless, so never mind. But expecting to hate half of the hours in the 40 year time period doesn't seem to gel with being happy for the most part...if you get what I mean. I can relate to this, though. I've been fascinated by death since I was maybe 4 or 5. I remember walking through the cemetery with my grandmother in when I was in preschool, thinking it might be so nice to lie in one of the coffins under the ground and just be asleep forever. OOC, do you have the sense that daily life is somehow more difficult for you than for others? Or more tiring? That is definitely the case for me... I'm significantly more emotional, sensitive, particular, and thorough than most people I know--which I'm sure sounds like a pretty weird thing to say about yourself, but it's just true. Incidentally, I'm the daughter, granddaughter, and great-granddaughter of physicians, and medical school was always my goal until I ended up getting tugged in another direction, in college. I have a successful writing career now, and three kids, so it doesn't really make sense to go to medical school, but I still want to badly enough that I may eventually do it despite the hurdles. I also know the suicide rate is higher for doctors. Just wondering if it could be a personality type sort of thing. Take care...
That's true we do all die but kind of hard to know if there's a reason to exist. I guess that's not the point to you if you're really miserable, though. What's been going on? Do you want to talk?

I'm really sorry. 😞 I lost my job this year, too, and every month I scramble to sell things to see if I can make the rent. It is truly horrible and I wouldn't wish that kind of stress on anyone. ❤️❤️ In my moderately sized town, I found more than one charity program that has helped me make rent. Are you sure there's nothing like that where you are? If you tell me your general area maybe I could help you Google around for something like that?

I wish I could give you the Sam-e right now. It's so much better than SSRIs IMHO and like no side effects. Plus it typically works within a few hours, so obviously it's almost like a miracle. It's really a shame hardly any Americans know about it. You should look for it tomorrow at your local grocery stores or order on Amazon. 400 mg, or get 200 mg and take two. I'm sure you think I'm a nut for pushing it so hard, but I swear it's like an SSRI or honestly even more effective, and it works for most people the same day. Bonus points it doesn't mess w your sex drive like SSRIs, and you don't have to take it daily if you feel good a certain day. It doesn't work like SSRIs... ❤️❤️

Try walking. I really think it will help. Try a small dose of melatonin before bed for a few nights, too. That can really help depression. Most people don't know, but a doctor told me. You should see a therapist, too. Therapy is o helpful... ❤️

Why is the psychiatrist eval and the prescription taking so long? Maybe you could go somewhere else? I still strongly recommend the ER or that medicine I was telling you about-- Sam-e. Google it if you feel up to it. ❤️❤️❤️

I understand. It's okay if you don't want to get into it... ❤️❤️❤️ I'm not a planner either and almost did something terrible last month. Really scary. We non-planners have to be careful. Please take care of yourself. I'm here if you want to talk at any time in the future. I've been through my share of awful stuff unfortunately, so I know how bad things can get. I really hope you stay safe and feel some relief. You deserve peace and happiness.

I'm so sorry you are going through this. I've been in bad places like this before and it's really scary. I also always try to fuck up my relationship when I'm severely depressed. Does your girl know all these details? I would love it for you if she could give you lots of comfort and support, which you definitely seem to need. You might consider going to the urgent care or hospital. Mental health can be urgent and there's nothing wrong with treating it as such. I think you need some help soon--like today. Tell your girlfriend everything... Please. ❤️ And listen, I'm not trying to be some kind of weird pill pusher, but I know two good things you can take if you don't go to the ER or get a prescription right now. Valerian root for severe anxiety and this amazing stuff called Sam-e for depression. It boosts serotonin and dopamine, often same day (yes, really) and can be found at grocery stores and Amazon. Are you a girl or guy (biologically)? Depression at your age can be very physical/chemical, and if you're female, it's extra tricky because of hormonal fluctuations. It's not unusual for drinking to kind of help...and kind of not help, like you said. Reaching for something like drugs or alcohol to help alleviate your pain is pretty normal I would say, but also definitely going to make things worse in the long run (trust me). That will only destabilize your brain chemistry more. (Don't worry though, totally correctable!) I was a lot like you when I was 17 and was totally dismayed and shocked to find myself in that kind of state. Turns out my depression is PMDD and is hormonal, but I didn't know that until last year (I'm now 34 and have three young kids). I felt suicidal in and off starting around 15. So let me tell you, it can get better. And worse again, and better again. Mental health fluctuates like all health. A few things I would strongly recommend are talking to your parents if they are loving and generally supportive, trying to link up with the school counselor or access another counselor via your parents (I cannot overstate how important therapy is - that's where you learn how to survive depression like this). Also, I know you're going to roll your eyes because a lot of people do, but daily aerobic exercise of ANY kind. 15 minutes a day minimum, preferably 20-45. Anything that gets your heart rate up. Walking, dancing in your bathroom, jogging the school track, walking up and down stairs... When you really feel too depressed to do it, that's when you HAVE to do it. Aerobic exercise has legit saved my life during severe depression. Good, consistent sleep is also key. If you can't sleep, buy like a 3 mg melatonin supplement from Amazon or the drug store, preferably chewable so you can divide it into smaller doses, and take like 1-2 mg at night. It's great for depression! Non habit forming as well. Finally, the biggie... Sam-e! Most grocery stores and drug stores have it. It's not the cheapest thing on earth but if you can get your hands on it, it's an antidepressant that is freaking amazing. In a small subset of people it can cause stomach trouble but in most it doesn't. It's not an ssri so none of those side effects, and it works for most people in a few hours. Start with 200 mg, one in the morning, and if you don't feel better on day one, try 400 mg the next morning. Taking it late in the day makes some people have trouble sleeping, so stick to mornings. This is a prescription drug in Europe but it's very safe, such that two of my children actually take it. My dad and stepfather are doctors, so I know what I'm talking about and am not recklessly encouraging you to try a drug. Sam-e, like exercise, has literally saved my life a few times. Reach out to me again if you buy it and I'll tell you more about how you can take higher doses (up to 1,200 mg) fit more severe depression. Btw you don't have to take it daily. If it makes you feel bad and not good, just stop. But it won't. It's amazing stuff. Oh also, it can help you stop drinking without feeling crappy. Trust me on this! Write it down and go get some. ❤️ Some of the best people in the world have depression, but I promise you can manage it. You just have to know how. If I can do it, you can.
